items.reason: The shell's cards reach the server through about 40 database functions taking the sign-in key (alerts and alert settings, browser alerts on/off and test alert, billing and receipts, entry machine numbers and machine orders, support access grant/end, member reports, plan requests, phone links, question and talk counts, trainer setup, member photos, gym state) plus three Worker addresses (public push key, billing checkout, online join payments). All functions are open to anon and work out the gym from the key; owner-only ones refuse a desk key: support access, billing and receipts, alert settings, adding or removing an entry machine. The desk may by design approve plan requests and phone links, give machine numbers, send machine orders and save member photos. Worker routes are judged in the server areas.

Every table these cards touch has row security on with no policy, so apps cannot read them directly; the gym check lives in the key functions. Other-gym tests: alerts and alert reads 0098 test 8f (another gym's owner gets NOT_FOUND and sees nothing); browser alerts 0076 test 2 (another gym's key sees off) and 9other; test alert 0095 1othergym; member photos 0043 test 7; plan requests 0044 5other and 6gymb; report requests 0045 6gymb; phone links 0048 2b and 2c; billing receipts 0063 7b; trainer, question and talk tables are proven in the screens-2 area. Missing: entry machine tables (no test of their own) and support access records (only a bad key is tried), both already open findings.

Rule applied. Entry machine tables (machines, members, commands) have no other-gym test: reused FN-L3-panel-screens-1-01. Support access records: reused FN-L3-panel-auth-data-03. Alert settings and gym state take no row id, so another gym's key can only reach its own gym. No new finding.
Rule applied: no live cross-gym attempt was run; only code, tests and the catalog were read.
No key pattern hit in this area. The browser-alert key is fetched from the server at run time (a public push key), not kept in code.
The shell holds no AI or paid-service key; billing checkout and online payments go through the Worker with the gym's own sign-in key.
Sign-in, PIN and brute force live in the auth area; the shell has no sign-in or sign-out code of its own (Welcome reuses the auth forms). The never-ending panel sign-in also covers every card here.

No raw HTML, eval or innerHTML in the shell; React escapes all text. HQ news buttons open only https addresses or app pages the role may open. WhatsApp links are built by the shared encoder; outside links carry noreferrer. A member's workout report CSV is re-written through a guard so a cell like =HYPERLINK opens as text. Machine orders are rebuilt on the server with a 40-letter name and fixed fields.

One upload: the desk's member photo (camera or picked file). The browser redraws it as a square JPEG on a canvas (drops anything hidden in the file); the server takes at most 100 KB, checks the JPEG start bytes, only for a live member of the key's own gym, stored as data not a file. Another gym's key cannot read or remove it (0043 test 7).

The new-gym page shows the gym code and join link (by design, to share); the code can be found by trying codes, an existing finding. The member card QR holds only the member id, read at the desk. Pay links point inside the app.
The shell imports only react, react-dom, qrcode-generator and the shared theme at run time; none has an alert. Vite and Vitest alerts are build and test tools; xlsx alerts belong to the import area.
